en: Oṃ, salutations to the illustrious Kubjikā.
Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Hsphreṁ Hsauṁ, I worship the sandals of the venerable Guru.
[Now, the procedure for the worship of the supreme Śrī Kujā is being written.]
Having performed the ritual sipping of water (ācamana) three times according to the triple principle (tritatva), one should then offer the arghya oblation to the Sun.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Rhrkṣrauṃ! To Kulamārttaṇḍabhairava, together with the Power of Radiance (Prakāśaśakti), [I offer] water for the hands (arghaṃ) and perform worship (pūjā). [This is the] recitation and hymn of praise (japastotra).
Aiṁ (5). You are the fierce sun that destroys the end brought about by the impurities of the Kali age; you are the formidable enemy of the hosts of the Kula of Rajas;
you are the bestower of knowledge and bliss. You are the most excellent delight for those who have transcended worldly existence, the progenitor, and the one with hands full of flowers and fruits.
I bow to Kulārka, the web of rays; obeisance to the flower for Kulamārttaṇḍa Bhairava.
Then, one should perform a salutation to the guru.
Aiṃ (5) O you whose form is the unbroken circle! Aiṃ (5) Worship of the feet of the supreme guru, Amukānandanātha.
Then, the flower-seat: Aiṁ, obeisance and worship to the lotus-seat (five times); Aiṁ, obeisance and worship to the leaf-seat (five times).

Aiṁ (5) to the Tortoise Seat, Pā Pū (5). Aiṁ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce to Koṅkaṇā, Hraḥ to the Weapon, Phaṭ. Lohale! The spreading away of spirits. Aiṁ (5) Hūṁ Phaṭ, O Vajra-Cage, Svāhā. The making of the vajra-enclosure. Aiṁ (5) O Caramakula, Kulacāmare, Aiṁ Hrīṁ Hūṁ Phaṭ Svāhā. The blocking of the ten doors.
Then one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa).
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkannāya Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ.
The purification of the hands.
Aiṃ (5) Homage to the Blessed One, the Lotus of the Heart! Hrāṃ, Śrī! To the two thumbs, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṁ (5) Hsphreṁ, to Kubjikā, the Island of the Kula; Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, to the two index fingers, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṁ (5) Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ Varvvaśikhe Śrīṁ Hūṁ; to the two middle fingers, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṁ (5) Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhi Bahurūpāyai Hraiṁ Śrī Anāmikābhyāṃ Pā Pū (5). Aiṁ (5) Chrāṁ Chrīṁ Mahantārikāyai Hrauṁ Śrī Kaniṣṭhābhyāṃ Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkannāya Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ. Pā Pū (5) with both palms and backs of the hands. Thus is the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*).
Aiṃ (5) Homage to the Blessed Lady, the Glorious One, to the Upper Face, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hsphreṃ, obeisance to Kubjikā for the eastern face, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Aiṃ, to the right face, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhī, [homage] to the venerable Northern Face, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śrāṃ Śrīṃ, to Mahantārikā, to the venerable Western Face, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkannāya Śrīparāparavaktrāya Pā Pū (5).
Thus ends the placement upon the mouth.
Aiṃ (5) Homage to the Blessed One, the Lady of the Heart-Lotus! Hrāṃ, homage to the glorious Heart! Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā, the Island of the Kula, Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, svāhā to the head; Pā Pū.
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Varvaraśikhe Hrūḥ Śrīśikhāyai Vauṣaṭ Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Ghore Aghore Aghorāmukhī Bahurūpāyai Hrai Śrī Kavacāya Hūṃ Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Chāṃ Chīṃ, obeisance with Vaṣaṭ to the three eyes of the venerable Mahantārikā; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkannāya Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ Pā Pū (5).
Thus ends the ritual placement upon the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
Then one should perform the placement of the bowl; having drawn a square mandala on the ground.

"Hrīṃ, salutation to the Foundation Power (Ādhāraśakti) and others"—thus [one prepares] the seat. Having washed [the vessel] with the Astra-mantra, having offered guggulu resin into the fire with the Aghora mantra, [one recites]:
"Hrīṃ, O Vajra-water, Hūṃ Phaṭ! One should fumigate with the Vajra [incense]. Having worshipped with sandalwood and other offerings...
Having placed it upon that ground, one should fill it with water while reciting the mantra "Namaḥ. Then follows the worship.
Aiṃ pā pū (5) || Hrīṃ pā pū (5) || Śrīṃ pā pū (5) || Hsphreṃ pā pū (5) || Hsauṃ pā pū (5) ||
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ, to Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, the Lord of Heroes, Śkṣmlvryīṃ, [offer] water-vessel, Pā Pū (5). Having worshipped with Hrāṃ and the others, beginning with the heart.
Perform the invocation and other rites; [offer] sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, and flowers with "Namaḥ"; then display the *dhenumudrā*.
The Gāyatrī.
Aiṃ (5). We know Kubjikā; we meditate upon her who is the island of the Kula; may that Kubjī inspire us.
Sprinkling that water upon the gods is an act of honoring them.
Thus is the procedure for placing the water vessel.
Again, the placement of the *argha* vessel: [the ritual] of the triangular *cakra* for the sake of the *thavana* (offering). This is the *sthāpanā-pūjā*.
Hrīṃ, obeisance to Ādhāraśakti and the others. Having washed these vessels for worship and the arghya water with the Astra-mantra, [place them] upon the mandala. Write "Laṃ" on each of them.
Oṃ, you who delight in the mantra, svāhā!
Oṃ! O Gaṅgā and Yamunā, indeed Goḍāvarī and Sarasvatī, Narmadā, Sindhu, and Kāverī—be present in this water.
The goad mudrā is for the invocation [of the deity] from the solar mandala at the confluence of the sacred bathing places (tīrtha).
Oṃ dhāra japaraye | Vajreṇa dhūpakena | Thus is the consecration of the water for respectful offering (arghāsthāpana).
Then follows the installation of the conch.
For the purpose of worship, one should fashion a triangular wheel adorned with the syllables *thava*, *khava*, *vasa*, *laṃ*, *khaṃ*, *na*, *hā*, *yā*, *va*.
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to the mandala of Śaṅkhadhāra. With the weapon-mantra (astramantra), for the purpose of establishing the Mañciserāva mandala. This is the offering. The mantra:
Oṃ maṃ, obeisance to the support of the conch, whose essence consists of the ten kalās of the fire-maṇḍala.
With the Astra-mantra, one removes the conch and the stone. Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ, I establish the conch.
[Pūjā]
Oṃ Aṃ! Homage to the conch vessel for the arghya offering, which is the solar disc consisting of twelve kalās.

*Laṃ khathanne* || *Blūṃ*, I fill with water; *namaḥ*. With the *Aṅkuśa-mudrā*, for the invocation of the holy waters (*tīrtha*), using the mantra *Oṃ Gaṅge...*. The worship (*pūjā*): *Oṃ*, *namaḥ* to the lunar disc (*somamaṇḍala*), the essence of the sixteen digits (*ṣoḍaśakalātman*), the nectar of the conch-offering (*śaṅkhārghāmṛta*).

Hsauṁ, obeisance to the goddess Varuṇā; śauṁ, obeisance to the goddess Varuṇādevī. One should bow to the unbroken grains and dūrvā grass placed upon the fire. One should fumigate with a thunderbolt [incense]. Having worshipped with the heart-mantra and others beginning with Hrāṁ, [one says] Vauṣaṭ.
For the purpose of the fish-seal (*matsyamudrā*): *vaṃ*, the cow-seal (*dhenumudrā*). For the purpose of the binding of the directions with three *tāra*s: [the mantra].
Having gathered the materials for the worship, including the *tho laṃkhanadhamano* [powder for marking], one recites the *Kubjigāyatrī*. Thus ends the installation of the conch (*śaṅkhasthāpana*).
Now follows the ritual for placing the water jar.
Having drawn a drop (bindu) and a triangle (trikoṇa) on one's left, the worship there is as follows:
Aiṃ (5) Raṃ, salutation to the fire mandala.
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkannāya Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ.
Having washed the jar with its mantra and having smeared it with red sandalwood paste.
Having established it within that maṇḍala, one should worship it.
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ, salutation to the solar disc.
Having thus worshipped, O Mistress of Vatsas, one should worship the jar while reciting the mantra. [This is] the worship.
Aiṁ (5) Saṁ, obeisance to the lunar maṇḍala. Worship of one’s chosen deity with the root mantra.
Then, having covered it with the fish-seal (matsyamudrā).
Aiṃ Plūṃ Hsauṃ Haṃ Saṃḥ! O Immortal One, born of the immortal, showerer of nectar, cause the nectar to flow; Svāhā!
Having recited this mantra ten times.
Aiṃ (5) Glūṃ Mlūṃ Plūṃ Slūṃ Nlūṃ, salutation to the Five Jewels (Pañcaratnā).

Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ Plūṃ Hsauṃ Haṃ Saḥ! O Immortal One (2)! O You who arise from the nectar of immortality, O Showerer of Nectar, cause the nectar to flow (2)! Sauṃ! O Sudhā, O Śukra, release the waters (2)! Burn the power and capacity of the fourfold *niyina* (2)! Manifest the Great *Khecarī* Mudrā (2)! Hūṃ Svāhā!
Aiṃ (5) Klāṃ Klīṃ Klūṃ Amṛte (2) Amṛtodbhave Amṛtavarṣiṇī Hrīṃ Amṛtaṃ Śrāvaya (2) Hrīṃ Sudhā (? Kṛṣṇaśrāpa Vimocaya (2) Kṛṣṇaśrāpamocakāyai Hūṃ (2) Svāhā.
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ (9) to Ānandabhairava, Saṃ (9) to Ānandabhairavī, Vauṣaṭ!
Having recited the root mantra seven times, one should display the *dhenu* and *yoni* mudrās; this is the ritual for the installation of the jar (*ghaṭasthāpana*).

(Purity: the fish-seal [mīnamudrā] is the purification of the family nectar. This is the section on the purification of substances. Now, the installation of the *argha* offering: having drawn a dot, a triangle, a circle, and a square.
Therein, one should worship as follows:
Aiṃ (5) Salutation to Kāmarūpa-pīṭha. Aiṃ (5) Salutation to Pūrṇagiri-pīṭha.
Aiṃ (5) Salutation to Jālandharapīṭha. Aiṃ (5) Salutation to Oḍiyānapīṭha.
Aiṁ (5) This is the worship. Aiṁ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkannāya Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ.
Having washed the support with this [mantra] and placed it within that mandala, one should worship it.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Rāṃ Rīṃ Rūṃ Rmlvryūṃ! To the fire-maṇḍala, whose self is the ten dharma-kalās, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5)! To Dhūmrā, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Raṃ, obeisance to Sūṣmā; Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Laṃ, obeisance to Jvālinī; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Vaṃ, obeisance and worship to Jvālinī. Aiṃ (5) Śaṃ, obeisance and worship to Visphuliṅginī. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Ṣaṃ, obeisance to Suśrī, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Saṃ, obeisance to Svarūpā, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ, obeisance and worship to Kapilā. Aiṃ (5) Laṃ, obeisance and worship to Havyavahā.
Aiṃ (5) Kṣaṃ, obeisance to Kavyavahā (pā pū 5).
Having thus worshipped the support, [one recites] the mantra for washing the vessel.
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkannāya Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ. Se! Le!
Aiṃ (5) Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hrūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarva Sarve Hraiṃ Juṃ Saḥ Hrauṃ, Rudrarūpe Hraḥ Pā Pū (5).
Having placed guggulu resin into the fire with this [mantra].
Aiṃ (5) Vajrakubjinī Hsphreṃ, the attractor of the three worlds; Hrīṃ, the dissolver of the limbs of desire; Klīṃ Strīṃ, the great agitator; Aiṃ Sauṃ Saḥ Pā Pū (5).
One should fumigate with this. One should recite the root mantra ten times. Aiṃ—protection with the weapon-mantra.
Enveloping with the Kavaca mantra; gazing with the Netra mantra; binding the directions; [applying] sandalwood paste and so forth.
Having worshipped with the six limbs including the root mantra, one should install it upon the support and worship it.
Aiṃ (5) Hāṃ Hīṃ Hūṃ Hmlvryūṃ, salutation to the Śrīpātra, which is the solar disc consisting of twelve kalās; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Kaṃ Bhaṃ, obeisance and worship to Tapinī. Aiṃ (5) Khaṃ Baṃ, obeisance and worship to Tāpinī.
Aiṃ (5) Gaṃ Phaṃ, obeisance and purification to Dhūmrā; Aiṃ (5) Ghaṃ Paṃ, obeisance and purification to Marīci.
Aiṃ (5) Ṅaṃ Naṃ to Jvālinī, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Caṃ Dhaṃ, obeisance to Rūcī; Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Chaṃ Daṃ, obeisance to Suṣumnā; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Jaṃ Thaṃ, obeisance to Bhogadāyī; Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Jhaṃ Taṃ, obeisance to Viśvā; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Ñaṃ Ṇaṃ, obeisance and worship to Bodhinī. Aiṃ (5) Ṭaṃ Ḍhaṃ, obeisance and worship to Dhāriṇī.
Aiṃ (5) Ṭhaṃ Ḍaṃ, obeisance to Kṣamā; Pā Pū (5).
Having thus worshipped the vessel, one should take the nectar (amṛta) residing in the jar, recite the root mantra, and fill the vessel with fish, meat, and so forth.
Aiṃ (5). One should offer as an arghya the great primordial nectar, produced from the fragments of the cosmic egg, arising from all the oceans, and filling [the vessel].
Aiṁ (5). I fill the Śrīpātra for the venerable Kubjikā; salutation.
Then one should worship Soma-karā.
Aiṃ (5) Sāṃ Sīṃ Sūṃ Smlvryūṃ, to the nectar of the Śrīpātra, whose essence is the Moon-maṇḍala consisting of sixteen digits, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Aṃ, to Amṛtā, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Āṃ, to Mādanā, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Iṃ, obeisance to Pūṣā, pā pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Īṃ, obeisance to Tuṣṭi, pā pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Uṃ, obeisance to Puṣṭi, pā pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Ūṃ, obeisance to Ratī, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Ṛṃ, obeisance to Dhṛti, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Ṝṃ, obeisance to Śaśinī, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Ḷaṃ to Candrikā, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Ḷḹṃ to Kāntā, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Eṃ, obeisance to Jyotsnā, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ, obeisance to Śrī, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Oṃ, obeisance to Prīti, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Auṃ. To Aṅgadā, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Aṃ. To Pūrṇā, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Aḥ, to Pūrṇāmṛtā, Pā Pū (5). Having thus performed the worship.
One should worship with the five jewels and recite the mantra.

Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ Plūṃ Hsauṃ Haṃ Saḥ Amṛte (2) Amṛtodbhave Amṛtavarṣiṇi Amṛtaṃ Śrāvaya (2) Svāhā. With this, one should recite [the mantra] three times. Phaṭ is for the inspection of characteristics. With the armor-mantra (kavaca), there is the veiling. Vauṣaṭ is for the gazing. One should recite again with the fish-mudrā (matsyamudrā).

Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Hsphreṁ Hsauṁ Hsauṁ Hsphreṁ Śrīṁ Hrīṁ Aiṁ! Come (2)! O Immortal One, born from the immortal, whose form is nectar (2)! Cause the nectar to flow (2)! Make it nectar (2)! Accept this dwelling (2)! Abandon all defects (2)! Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ Hraiṁ Hrauṁ Hraḥ! For the sake of Śiva, Hra Phaṭ! Namaḥ Svāhā!
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ (9) Ānanda Bhairavāya Saṃ (9) Ānandabhairavī Vauṣaṭ. Śukraśrāpavimocaya (2) Śukraśrāpamocakāyai Svāhā. Thus one should recite.
Having dissolved [the offering] with the Trikūṭa-mudrā, having written the syllable Aiṃ in the center of the vessel, [recite] the mantra.

Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Prasphura (2) Ghora (2) Taratanu (2) Rupacata (2) Pracaṭa (2) Kaha (2) Vama (2) Dama (2) Ghātaya (2) Vighātaya (2) Vighna (2) Hūṃ Hūṃ Hūṃ Phaṭ Kroṃ Śrīkaumārikā Vicce Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Saṃ (9), O Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda Śrī Mahāvidyārājeśvarī Haṃ (9), [this is] for the venerable Arghapātra, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṁ (5) Having worshipped the heart and the other limbs with Sāṁ.
Having offered sandalwood, flowers, and consecrated rice.
Aiṃ (5). Homage to the Blessed One Hsphreṃ Kubjikā! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ! O Terrible One, O Non-terrible One, O You Whose Face is Non-terrible! Chāṃ chīṃ! Kiṇi (2)! Vicce! Pā pū (5)!

Having recited this mantra seven or ten times, one should display the *yonimudrā*; this is the procedure for placing the vessel. [Next is] the placement of the *argha* vessel for the retinue and the vessel for enjoyments (*bhoga*).
Then follows the purification of the elements (bhūtaśuddhi).
aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsphreṃ hsauṃ hsauṃ hsphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ ||
Then follows the self-worship.
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, the Lord of Heroes, Śkṣmlvryīṃ! To the Self, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṁ, sandalwood—pā pū (5). Hrīṁ, unbroken rice—pā pū (5). Śrīṁ, heroic ash and vermilion—pā pū (5). Hsphreṁ, the enchantress of all people—pā pū (5). Hsauṁ, flowers—pā pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda Vīrādhipataye ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ PĀ PŪ (5) || Aiṃ (5) KṢSAUṂ PĀ PŪ (5) || Satiation on the head with the Bindu.
Then, having performed the internal sacrifice.
Having awakened the Goddess by means of the instruction of the Guru beginning with the syllable Aiṃ, one should place her upon the mandala.
Aiṃ (5) Flower, Pā Pū (5) || Aiṃ, accept the bali (2), svāhā ||
Aiṃ (5). One should recite the Mālinī [mantra].
Then one should offer the five-fold oblation (pañcabali).
Aiṃ (5). To the one seated on a peacock throne, Pā Pū (5). Meditation.
Aiṃ (5). Resembling a hibiscus flower in hue, adorned with red garments, seated upon a peacock throne, and wearing a snake as a sacred thread.
Three-eyed, with tawny hair standing erect, likewise holding a sword and the *pheṭaka* weapon, and bearing a lute, a skeleton, a trident, and a *khaṭvāṅga* staff.
[One should worship] the God holding a vessel of drops (bindupātra), as well as Kṣetrapāla and Baṭuka.
Homage to the one whose flower is meditative concentration.

Aiṃ (5). O Devīputra Baṭukanātha, Mahākapila, you who shine with three matted locks, three-eyed one, Jvālāmukha, descend (2)! Come, come, O Blessed One, into the midst of the maṇḍala; accept the offering as it has been presented (2);
grant the desired object, Hūṃ (3) Phaṭ Svāhā!
Flower and offering for the *baṭuka*: Aiṃ (5) Narāsanāya Pā Pū (5).
Meditative absorption.
Aiṁ (5): Mounted upon a great preta, endowed with a dark-red complexion, holding a sword and a shield in his hands, and likewise a skull-cup and a khaṭvāṅga staff.
The god who wears a garland of severed heads, radiant with formidable fangs,
the Great God with hair standing erect, with tawny eyebrows and tawny eyes.
Salutations to you, Mahādeva, of terrible form, the protector of the sacred field (kṣetrapālaka).
The flower of meditative concentration, Pā Pū. (5)
Aiṃ (5). O Lord of Installation, come here! Descend into this center of the maṇḍala according to your name!

You who have four arms and three eyes, who hold a khaṭvāṅga, a sword, and a shield, who carry a trident in your hand, who are adorned with a garland of great skulls, and whose radiance is equal to millions of lightning flashes—come, come, O Blessed One!
O you in the form of Bhairava, accept this offering of food as it has been presented; destroy my obstacles! Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā! Thus is the bali. [Thus is] the field.
Aiṃ (5), for the lion throne, Pā Pū (5).
Meditative absorption.
Aiṃ (5). She has the luster of molten gold, can assume any form at will, and is in the prime of youth;
she possesses a form that is intoxicated, yet is a skeleton adorned with all ornaments.
Adorned with hands holding the *liṅga*, the noose, the skull-bowl, and the goad,
and seated upon a corpse, she grants the fulfillment of all desires and aims.
The flower of meditative concentration, PĀ PŪ. (5)

Aiṁ (5). Whosoever among the Yoginīs are born of the *pīṭhas*, born of the *kṣetras*, innate (*sahaja*), born of yoga, born of mantra, born of the womb, or born of the *kula*; whosoever among the Yoginīs are the sky-farers (*khecarī*), earth-farers (*bhūcarī*), ground-farers (*gocarī*), those of one syllable, two syllables, three syllables, four [syllables]...
O you who dwell in the three worlds, consisting of five, six, seven, eight, or nine syllables, accept this bali-offering of food as it has been provided; grant me success! Hūṃ Phaṭ Svāhā!
Thus [is] Bali. [Thus is] Yoginī.
Aiṃ (5) Pretāsana Pā Pū (5) ||
Meditative concentration.
Aiṁ (5). She is of terrible form and exceedingly fierce, of wrathful form and most wrathful;
with a face made formidable by fangs, she stands upon a corpse.
The goddess is fleshless, the Night of Time (Kālarātrī), adorned with a garland of severed heads;
she holds a sword and a scimitar, and bears a hand-drum and a skull-topped staff.
She holds a skull in her hand and likewise bears a vessel of nectar;
she is tawny, with reddish-brown hair, reddish-brown eyebrows, and reddish-brown eyes.
Her limbs adorned with all kinds of ornaments and decorated with bone ornaments,
with hair standing erect and deformed in appearance, Cāmuṇḍā is the Supreme Sovereign.
The flower of meditative concentration, phat pūḥ. (5)
Aiṁ (5) Hskhphreṁ, accept this bali offering for the illustrious Siddhicāmuṇḍā! Svāhā! Thus [is] the bali.
Cāmuṇḍā.
Aiṃ (5) Mūṣāsana Pā Pū (5) ||
Meditative concentration.
Aiṃ (5). To the Lord of Gaṇas, Gajavaktra, who resembles a conch, a lotus, and the moon;
who is mounted upon the seat of a crucible; the three-eyed Supreme Lord.
Salutations to the one who has become the king of elephants, [bearing] a rosary for recitation, an axe, a vessel for the *bindu*, and likewise a snake as a sacred thread.
The flower of meditative concentration, Pāpū. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaiṃ Gauṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ! O Śrī Kulagaṇeśvara, accept this offering (bali)! Svāhā! Thus [is] the offering. Gaṇeśa.
The invocation and so forth, with sandalwood paste, unbroken rice, incense, and lamps—this is the worship (pūjā). (5)
One should display the great mudrās of the threatening gesture, the staff, the womb, and the elephant; [one should perform] the satiation with the bindu.
Aiṃ (5) Kṣsauṃ Pā Pū (5) ||
Recitation and Hymn of Praise.

Aiṃ (5). With flowers and other offerings, incense, lamps, betel, honey, and oblations, I worship with devotion Kumāra, the son of Gaurī, whose body is like the sky; the Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapa); the Yoginīs; Cāmuṇḍā in her fierce form; Gaṇeśa, who wears two turbans and removes obstacles.
May the Lord of the Wheel, who destroys the misfortunes of those who worship him, grant both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Here [are offered] perfumes and so forth; and for the purification of the mouth, betel-leaf and other items according to the ritual convention.
O Goddess, the fivefold [elements] swallowed are the chewing of the causal banner;
O Goddess, this is the purification of the pure, the infinite purification of the breath.
Purification || Libation ||
Aiṃ (5). Seated upon a throne of *pretas*, Bhairava—who removes the fear of worldly existence—is the embodiment of mantra, accompanied by Caṇḍī and Caṇḍī;

the world-protectors with their prostrating serpent-hoods, the lords of serpents, the *yakṣas*, *rakṣasas*, and *daityas*, together with the hosts of ancestors, the Mothers, the guardians of the fields (*kṣetrapālas*), and the *yoginīs* joined in yoga.
May those who move on land, in water, and in the sky drink this nectar.
May all the deities, the oceans, and the Vināyakas drink;
may the Yoginīs and Kṣetrapālas likewise be established within my body.
The body shall be indestructible, free from old age and death;
there shall be no disease, grief, or fear, and there shall be royal splendor and abundant prosperity.
Aiṃ (5) Salutation to Śrīnātha. Aiṃ (5) Salutation to Śrīsiddhinātha.
Aiṃ (5). Homage to the illustrious Kujeśanātha. One should perform the formal acceptance.
Thus ends the ritual procedure for the five bali offerings.
Then follows the worship of the deities and the invocation.

Aiṁ (5). Having arisen at the wheel of sustenance (*dhāra-cakra*), having caused those [energies] residing in the mind-stone to descend into the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*), and having led them into the heart-lotus—[there she is] like a crystal, resembling a mass of intensely radiant light.
By meditating upon that eternal one, Kujā arises from it, possessing the three forms, both gross and subtle.
That Goddess, carrying the fire within the internal sacrifice, is meditated upon as being in the center of the wheel.
One should touch the god and the goddess.
Aiṃ (5). Within the circle of the illustrious Saṃvarta, O Subhīmā, you whose power is bliss established through the sequential steps;
there is the group of four in the Sṛṣṭi-nyāya, another group of five belonging to the Kula and Akula, and a group of six.
Furthermore, there are four pentagons, and from that, again four [triangles]; such is this mandala.
Bow down to that excellent guru, Śrī Kujeśa Bhairava, by whom [all things] are intermingled.
Thus is the invocation.
Then follows the worship.
Aiṃ (5) Alūṃ, O Śrī Anantamaṇḍala Ādideva, pā pū (5). With this, [offer] the bali.
Aiṁ (5) Haṁ (9). To Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda, the Lord of Heroes, śkṣmlvryīṁ, Pā Pū (5). With this, [offer] the bali.
Then follows the worship of the three deities.
Aiṃ (5) Narāsana Pā Pū (5) ||
Meditative absorption.
Aiṃ (5). The deity is seated upon a corpse-throne, blue in color and having one face.
The deity has three eyes and eight arms, holding a sword and a shield, a hand-drum and a skull-topped staff, and bearing a dot and a skull-cup.
Indeed, the skull-ornament is the limb of adornment for the field-protector who is meditating.
The flower of meditative concentration, Pā Pū. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Trauṃ! To the goddess Puṣparadvīpadanturā, the Kṣetrapāla who upholds the Vedas, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Prauṃ! To the Kṣetrapāla of the Śukla field, [who possesses] the speed of a horse from the island of Āśava and the goddess Vegā, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ!
O Śrīyivāhāra, Sovereign of the Great Abode, Hvjmyrūṃ! O Śrī Meghabhāsura Mahākṣetrapāla, Kapilaugra, resplendent with a mass of matted locks, three-eyed, Jvālāmukha, descend! Descend! (2)
In the form of Bhairava, seize! *turu* (2), *muru* (2), *la* (2), *kha* (2), devour! O Lord of the Great Āḍāmala, forgive me, you who grant boons; svāhā!
Aiṃ (5) Kṣāṃ kṣīṃ kṣūṃ kṣaḥ, obeisance to Kṣetrapāla (5).
Thus, accept the offering, svāhā! [This is] the staff mudrā. [The field.]
Aiṃ (5). Mayūrāsana. Pā pū (5). Meditation.
Aiṃ (5): [I bow to] the Youth in the form of a child, mounted upon a great peacock, whose limbs are adorned with red skulls, and who holds a staff and a spear in his two hands.
The glorious one, adorned with red garments, forms the bindu-mudrā with his hand;
thus should one constantly meditate upon Baṭuka, the son of noble family.
The flower of meditative concentration, Pā Pū. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, to Kulaputra Baṭukanātha, Pā Pū (5).
Thus [is] the Bali [offering]; [then] the Tarjanī-mudrā.
Aiṃ (5) [to] Mūṣāsana, Pā Pū (5).
Meditative absorption.
Aiṁ (5): Seated upon a rat-back throne, with a radiant white body and an elephantine face, possessing three eyes, he holds an axe, a sweetmeat ball, and a rosary of rudrākṣa beads.
Having thus meditated upon Maheśvara as Gaṇanātha, who wears a serpent as a sacred thread, who destroys all evils, and who removes obstacles;
The flower of meditative concentration, Pā Pū. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaiṃ Gauṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ, obeisance to Kulagaṇeśvara. Pā Pū (5).
Thus is the bali offering; [followed by] the elephant mudrā. This concludes the worship of the three deities.
Then, the three purifications: Aiṃ (5) to the lotus seat, Pā Pū (5). Meditation.
Aiṃ (5). She who says "I am yellow" is white; she possesses the lineage of the three transverse gurus, beginning with one's own guru, friend, and so forth.
Holding a staff, a face, and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, her body is of divine splendor.
Adorned with the beauty of jewel ornaments, she is the Guru, the Supreme Śiva, whose form is identical to that of Brahmā and Viṣṇu.
Having thus meditated upon Your form, which removes the fear of the world and possesses triple purity, I bow to You.
The flower of meditative concentration: PĀ PŪ (5). The worship.
Aiṃ (5). Svaguru Tūṣṇīśānandadeva, pā pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) [I worship] the feet of the supreme Guru Caryānandadeva (5).
Aiṃ (5). Homage to the supreme preceptor, the venerable Śrī Mitrānandadeva. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Hkṣmlvryaṃ. To the venerable Lord of the Threefold Purity, pā pū (5).
This is the *bali* offering. One should display the lotus, conch, trident, and cow (*dhenu*) mudrās. Thus is the triple purity (*triśuddhi*).
Then, from the guru-maṇḍala, the worship of the Ninefold Self (Navātma) and the extraction of the maṇḍala (cakra-uddhāra).

The Vedic peak is indeed triangular; furthermore, it is fixed as the fire of the *cāṇḍāla*, the fire of the *yuga*, or the external fourfold one. It has gates facing the directions of the oceans and is entirely garlanded with flames.
Situated within the center of that wheel is the boat for crossing existence (*bhavataraṇa*), which is the very form of Devananda himself.
I bow to you, who are named Bhairava, the sovereign of the three worlds, saluted by all, and joined with Kubjikā.
One should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) as follows:
Now follows the ritual placement of the Ṛṣis and the meters (ṛṣicchandanyāsa).
Aiṃ (5). To the sage Sadyojāta, homage for this Navātmākūṭarājamantra; [to the head].
Aiṃ (5). Homage to the aforementioned metre. [It is] in the mouth.
Aiṃ (5). Salutation to the deity Navātma-Kubjikā; [place] at the heart.
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ (9) Bījāyai namaḥ. [Salutation] to Bījā at the secret place.
Aiṃ (5) Saṃ (9). Homage to Śakti at the feet.
(5) Homage to Kīlaka! Sa (*?
Aiṃ (5) Hsaṃ to the two thumbs; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Kṣmaṃ to the two index fingers; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Lvaṃ to the two middle fingers; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṁ (5) Ryaṁ to the two ring fingers; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṁ (5) Ūṁ; to the two little fingers, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Aṃ, Phaṭ to the weapon. [This is] the hand-assignment (*kara-nyāsa*).
Aiṃ Hsaṃ, obeisance to the heart; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Kṣmaṃ, svāhā to the head; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Lvaṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Ryaṃ kavacāya hūṃ pā pū (5) ||
Aiṃ (5) Ūṃ, Vaṣaṭ to the Eye; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Aṃ, Phaṭ to the weapon; Pā Pū (5).
Thus ends the ritual placement upon the limbs (aṅganyāsa).
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ at the location of the crest-lock; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Saṃ, at the location of the head, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Kṣaṃ, on the forehead, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Maṃ, for the face, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Laṃ, for the heart, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Vaṃ at the navel, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Raṃ at the secret place, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Yaṃ on the two knees, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Ūṃ on the two feet, Pā Pū (5).
Thus ends the Nyāsa of the Ninefold Self. Again, the Karāṅganyāsa (the ritual placement on the hands and limbs).
Then follows the worship.
Aiṃ (5) Nlūṃ O Pūjā! To the Śrī Kubjikā of the Guru-maṇḍala, Pā Pū (5). [This is] in the center below the triangle.

Aiṁ (5) mlūṁ e, to the Great Worship, to the Śrīśakti of the Guru-maṇḍala, pā pū (5). [This is] in the east, at the edge of the Vedas. Aiṁ (5) plūṁ u, to the Supreme Guru-maṇḍala, to the Śrīdivyā, pā pū (5). [This is] in the south.
Aiṃ (5) Slūṃ, obeisance to the assembly of supreme gurus, to the venerable Jñānā; [perform] worship (pā pū). (5) In the north.
Aiṃ (5) Glūṃ Aḥ, to the venerable Ājñākusuma of the circle of gurus, pā pū (5). [In the west.]
Outside of that, in the Vedāmra.
Aiṃ (5) Śrīśivatatvagurumaṇḍala Parāyai Pā Pū (5) || To the East.
Aiṃ (5) Śrīvidyā-tattva-guru-maṇḍala-parāparāyai Pā Pū (5). [Offering] to the South.
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Ātmatattva-gurumaṇḍala, obeisance to Aparā (5). [To be performed] in the north.
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Ājñākusumāya Pā Pū (5). [In the west.]
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Jayāyai Pā Pū (5). In that mandala, in the southeast corner.
Aiṃ (5) Śrīvijayāyai Pā Pū (5) || In the southwest.
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Ajitāyai Pā Pū (5) || In the northwest.
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Aparājitāyai Pā Pū (5) || [To] Īśāna.
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ Śāntyatītāyai Pā Pū (5). [This is] in the middle half of the triangle; again, on the outer three spokes.
Aiṃ (5) Yaṃ for peace; Pā Pū (5) in the east.
Aiṃ (5) Raṃ, for Vidyā, Pā Pū (5). [In the] south.
Aiṃ (5) Vaṃ, for the Foundation, Pā Pū (5). In the north.
Aiṃ (5) Laṃ, to Nivṛtti, Pā Pū (5), in the west.
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Kulabhairavāya Pā Pū (5), in that maṇḍala, in the southeast.
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Kulanāthabhairavāya Pā Pū (5) || [To] the South-West.
Aiṃ (5) Śrīkulatumburubhairavāya Pā Pū (5). [In the northwest.]
Aiṃ (5) Pā Pū to the venerable Kulakapāṭabhairava in the northeast.
Aiṃ (5) Śrīkula-ājñābhairavāya pā pū (5). [In the right triangle.]
Aiṃ (5) Śrīkula Ājñā Devī pā pū (5). [In the left triangle.]
Outside of that is the eight-cornered [figure].
Aiṃ (5) Kṣāṃ Kṣīṃ Kṣūṃ Kṣaḥ, to the Guardian of the Field (Kṣetrapāla), Pā Pū (5). [In the southeast.]
Aiṃ (5) Gāṃ Gīṃ Gūṃ Gaḥ Glauṃ, obeisance (pā pū) (5) to Śrī Kulagaṇeśvara in the southwest (naiṛtye).
Aiṃ (5) Śrīṃ Hrīṃ, obeisance to Kulaputra Baṭukanātha, Pā Pū (5). [In the] northwest.
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Mahākaumārikā Vicce Pā Pū (5) || [To be placed] in the Īśāna direction.
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ (9) Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Jvālāyai Pā Pū (5). In the center of the triangle.
Aiṁ (5) for the lotus seat, pā pū (5). Aiṁ (5) for the seat of flowers beginning with the support (ādhāra).
Aiṃ (5). For the corpse-seat, Pā Pū (5). Meditation.
Aiṁ (5). Seated upon a corpse in the lotus posture, with ten faces and three eyes, having the color of the sky, greatly radiant, and endowed with all forms of protection.
The eastern face is golden-colored, the southern is adorned with black,
the northern should be yellow, and the one above that is dyed red.
To the right of the red [color] is the smoky-colored, and to the north is the white;
above that is the yellow color, and to the right of the yellow is the black.
They say that red is superior, while white above that is most excellent;
[one should meditate on] the ten-armed Lord, adorned with a garland of headless trunks, [holding] weapons.
The god holds a sword and a *pheṭa*, as well as a trident and a hook,
a sacred thread, an excellent water-pot, a hand-drum, and a skull-topped staff.
He holds an arrow well-joined to a bow, which is beautifully adorned with bells;
he also holds a discus and a mace in his hands, while his other hands display the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
The corpse, bearing the *bindu* on its forehead and adorned with various ornaments, should be yellow in color and seated comfortably upon the throne.
Thus, by meditating upon this ninefold mandala of form— the guru-mandala—
with a disciplined mind, human beings quickly attain accomplishment.
May the flowers of meditative concentration purify all evil. (5)
Aiṁ (5). O Blessed One, to the Lord Navātma of the Guru-maṇḍala: come here (2)—this is the invocation. Stay here (2)—this is the stabilization.
For here, indeed, is presence; here is the act of bringing near. Here is cessation; here is the act of ceasing.
Aiṁ (5).
Hūṁ, for the armor; the act of armoring. The veiling. The binding of the directions with the weapon-mantra.

Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ. To the venerable Guru-maṇḍala and the Navātma and Navātmī, [I offer] water for the feet; *namaḥ* pā pū (5). Likewise, water for sipping (*ācamanīya*), the respectful offering (*argha*), the bath (*snāna*), and the bath with wine (*alisnāna*).
Sandalwood, vermilion, the enchanting one, flowers, three handfuls.
Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ Hskṣmlvryūṃ! To Ānandaśaktibhairava, the blissful Lord of Viras, Śkṣmlvryīṃ! To the venerable Navātman of the Śrī Gurumaṇḍala, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ Ānandaśaktibhairavānanda Śrīmahāvidyārājeśvarī Haṃ (9) [to] the venerable Lord of the Śrī-guru-maṇḍala, PĀ PŪ (5).
Thus is the Bali offering. [Next is] the Triśūlayoni mudrā.
Aiṃ (5) Aghore Hrāṃ, Thaghore Hrīṃ, Ghoraghorantare Hrūṃ Phreṃ, Sarvataḥ Sarvva Sarvve Hraiṃ Juṃ Saḥ Hrauṃ Rudrarūpe Hraḥ. Śrī Śikhāsvacchandamahābhairavā Pā Pū (5).
In the right triangle.
Aiṃ (5) Vajrakubjinī Hsphreṃ Trailokyakarṣaṇī Hrīṃ Kāmāṅgadrāvaṇī Klīṃ Strīṃ Mahākṣobhakāriṇī Aiṃ Sauṃ Saḥ Pā Pū (5). [In the left of the triangle.]
Aiṃ (5) Homage to the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā! Hrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ! O Terrible One, O Non-terrible One, O You Whose Face is Non-terrible!
Chāṃ chīṃ! Kiṇi (2)! Vicce! Pā pū (5)! [This is at the tip of the triangle.]
Thus, the offering with the six limbs and likewise the bali.

Aiṃ (5) O you who are the seat of all mantras, the lion-throne seat, the seats and sub-seats, the fields and sub-fields, the gathering places and sub-gathering places, the divine accomplishments, and the wheel of the pledge! Pā pū (5) Accept this offering! Svāhā! (2)
Aiṁ (5). Whatever has been said or not said, all that is for the Śrī-hṛdaya, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ, O ninefold self, accept this food offering and bali; svāhā!
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ! O you who are the essence of the ninefold mandala of the Gurus, accept this bali offering! Svāhā! (2)
Aiṃ (5) ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ! O Goddess of the Navātman of the Guru-maṇḍala, accept this bali offering! Svāhā! (2)

Aiṃ (5) ŚKṢMLVYĪṂ, accept this *bali* offering for the Goddess Navātmī of the Guru-maṇḍala; Svā Aiṃ. Candana, protect, purify (5). Hrīṃ, heroic unhusked rice (*akṣata*), protect, purify (5). Śrī-vīrabhasma, protect, purify (5). Hsphreṃ, Vīramohanī, protect, purify (5). Hsauṃ, heroic flower (*vīrapuṣpa*), protect, purify (5).
Aiṁ (5) Alibali palalārā pū (5) || Aiṁ (5) Vīradhūpaṃ pā pū (5) ||
Aiṁ (5), the hero’s lamp, pā pū (5). Aiṁ, the lotus mudrā.
Hrīṃ: the cow-seal (dhenumudrā). Śrīṃ: the parasol-seal (chatramudrā). Hsphreṃ: the womb-seal (yonimudrā).
One should display the *kādyamudrā* with the syllable *hsauṃ*. [This is] the libation (*tarpaṇa*).
Aiṃ (5) Salutation to the illustrious Nātha. Aiṃ (5) Salutation to the illustrious Siddhinātha.
Aiṃ (5) Homage to the illustrious Kujeśanātha; Aiṃ (5) Kṣsauṃ Pā Pū (5).
[Thus ends the morning ritual for the worship of the nine-fold Śrī Guru-maṇḍala according to the tradition of the Śrī Paścima-jeṣṭhānujeṣṭhā.]
Then, at midday, one should begin the worship of the ritual action and the worship of the cakra.

Aiṁ Hrīṁ Śrīṁ Hsphreṁ Hsauṁ Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ Hūṁ Hūṁ! O Vajramaṇḍala, O Vajriṇī, O Amoghā, O Mahāghorā, O Gaganaviśuddhā, purify [me]! (2) O Vajrāsana, Pā Pū (5) || (5) || This is the seat for one’s own self.
Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ Phaṭ Hsī Hsphreṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ: O radiant one, purifier of the orb of the sun! Aiṃ (5) Mārttaṇḍamaṇḍalaśodhanī Tejasvinī Hūṃ Phaṭ Hsī Hsphreṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ.
Scattering flowers into the sky.
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkannāya Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ. Lohele! Expulsion of the spirits.
Aiṁ hūṁ phaṭ vajrapañjare svāhā. This is the vajrīkaraṇa (the rite of making [oneself] into a vajra).
Aiṁ (5) cala-makule kula-macale hrīṁ hūṁ phaṭ svāhā. This is the sealing of the ten gates.
Now I shall fully explain the conclusion; one should commence the ritual worship.
One should perform the placement of the six limbs, beginning with the heart and so forth, as well as the thirty-two-fold placement.
The knotted [scripture], the twelve limbs, the six limbs, and the ritual placement (nyāsa);
Mālinī, Śabdarāśi, the six messengers (ṣaṭdūtī), and the five jewels.
The Navātman [mantra] with the Aghorāstra, the Mekākṣarī with the Trividyā,
the Ghorāstraka with the Triṣaṇḍā, and the Aghora with the five seed-syllables (bījapañcaka).
One should likewise perform the Praṇava; this is declared as the sixfold assignment (ṣoḍhā-nyāsa).
Without these assignments, O Goddess, there can indeed be no ritual worship.
Another method: Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the six faces, the twelve limbs, and the six limbs;

having placed Mālinī, the mass of sounds (*śabdarāśi*), which crosses over the fear of existence (*bhava*), for those who possess the three knowledges (*trividyā*); having placed the eight forms of Ghoryā and the six messengers (*ṣaḍdūtī*), which remove many evils; and having placed the five jewels (*ratnapañca*) at the knot of the *klīṃ* syllable—the hands are to be placed upon the fingers.
May the Navātman, the state of moving through the sky, protect [us]—it is the sixteen-fold ritual placement (ṣoḍhāṅganyāsa).
Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkannāya Hra (2) Astrāya Phaṭ.
Aiṁ (5). Homage to the Blessed Lady Hṛtkamalā! Hrīṁ Śrīṁ. To the two thumbs, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṁ (5) Hsphreṁ, to Kubjikā, the Island of the Kula; Hrīṁ Śrīṁ, to the two index fingers, Pā Pū (5).

Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Ruḥ Hsauṃ, obeisance to Ghoramukhā at the secret place; Pā Pū (5) at the secret place.
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Phaṭ Bhīme Hsauṃ, [salutation] to the one named Bhīmā on the right arm; Pā Pū (5), from Javarāha.
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Bhīṣaṇe Devyā Hsauṃ Bhīṣaṇāyai, on the left arm, Pā Pū (5).
From the eater of raw flesh.
Aiṃ (5) Hsauṃ Hrīṃ Saṃ Haḥ Vama Hsauṃ; for Nāmavāmanī, on the right foot, Pā Pū (5).
Java ḷ || Aiṁ (5) Hrīṁ Phaṭ! Drink, O Hsauṁ! For the one who drinks, at the left thigh, Pā Pū (5) || Khava ḷ ||
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ (9). To the venerable Ghorikāṣṭaka-nyāsa-bhaṭṭārikā, Pā Pū (5). Worship at the head.
And likewise the offering.
Having meditated daily upon the eightfold Ghorāṣṭaka, which destroys the five great sins,
one constantly attains peace and accomplishment for the pacification of planetary influences and epilepsy.
All faults will be pacified; it is the liberation from all sins.
And the fruit [of this]. Thus is the Ghorāṣṭaka placement (nyāsa).
Then follows the placement of the six syllables (ṣaḍdūtīnyāsa).

Aiṃ (5) Kāli Kāli Kāli Mahākālī, consumer of flesh and blood! Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ! O Goddess with red and black faces, may enemies not behold me! O messenger of the heart of Śrī, [protect] my heart! Pā Pū (5). [To the heart.]

Aiṃ (5). Homage to the Blessed Lady, the beloved Cāmuṇḍālī, consumer of blood, blood, and flesh, bearer of the skull-cup and the khaṭvāṅga staff! Strike (2)! Burn (2)! Blow (2)! Cook (2)! Devour my enemies (2)! Slay (2)! Hūṃ (3) Phaṭ! O Śrīśirodūtī, for the head, svāhā! For the head! (5) || For the head! ||
Aiṃ (5) Hsphrāṃ Hsphrīṃ Hsphrūṃ, Śrī-Śikhādūtī at the crest-lock, Pā Pū (5) Milikhāsa.
Aiṃ (5). Having lifted up, she pervades all the worlds; she is the primordial one, the illuminator, the one who is written upon by all the gods.
She is Śrī Kavacadūtī, the protectress within the armor, *pā pū* (5). [She has] two arms.
Aiṃ (5) Rakte (2) Mahārakte Cāmuṇḍeśvari, descend (2) Svāhā! O Śrī Netradūtī, protect (5) my eyes! Netranigaḍa (2)!

Aiṁ (5) Guhyakubjike hūṁ phaṭ! Destroy all my misfortunes—those [caused] by the application of yantras, mantras, powders, and so forth, whether they were made, caused to be made, will be made, or are being made by anyone; destroy them all! Daṃṣṭrākalālī hreṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ phaṭ! O Guhyakubjike, O Śrī Astradūtī, for the weapon: phaṭ! Pā!
PŪ (5). With the left foot, strike the ground three times (3) with the water from the *arghapātra* and *ambupātra* vessels;

then rotate [the hand] over the head at the "khādakāṣṭa" [point]. AIṂ (5) SAṂ (9) to the Six Messengers (*Ṣaḍdūtī*), the Noble Lady of the Deposition (*Nyāsabhaṭṭārikā*): PĀ PŪ. Perform worship upon one's own head. Likewise, offer the *bali*. Thus is the deposition of the Six Messengers (*Ṣaḍdūtīnyāsa*).
The fruit of the heart-mantra and others is the destruction of fear from enemies;
it bestows the fruit of mantra-siddhi and brings about the exhaustion of all sins.
She is the deluder of all tantras and the giver of knowledge regarding the rising of the breath and other such matters;
for she is always independent and the crusher of all weapons.
The fruit of the ritual placement (nyāsa).

Aiṁ (5). Vāgīśvarī, Glūṁ, she who has entered the womb of the Ratna-gagaṇaloka; O Gagaṇaloka, you who move in the nectar [of immortality]; O Gagaṇānanda-deva, O Gagaṇā; the sixty-four lakṣa-crores of Siddhis, the sixty-four lakṣa-crores of Yoginīs, Pā Pū (5). [To be placed] on the forehead.

Aiṁ (5). To Māyā: Mlūṁ. O you who enter the womb of the enjoyments of the jewel-like heavenly world; O you who move through the nectar of the heavenly world; O Goddess who grants the bliss of heaven; O Mother of Heaven; O Protectress of ten million Siddhis; O Yoginī of a hundred thousand times ten million; Pā Pū (5). [The two syllables] Nā and Śi are at the mouth.

Aiṃ (5). Mohanī Plūṃ! You who enter the womb of the enjoyments of the world of the Jewel-Wind; O world of the Jewel-Wind, you who circulate the nectar! O Pavanānanda-deva, O Pavanāmbā! You who possess sixteen crores of protectors, you who possess sixteen hundred thousand crores of Yoginīs! Pā Pū (5). [At the throat.]

Aiṁ (5). To Jñānā; mlūṁ. O you who enter the womb of the enjoyments of the jewel-like mortal world, O you who move through the nectar of the mortal world, O Goddess who grants bliss to mortals, O Mother of Mortals, O you of eight hundred thousand and ten million siddhis, O you of eight hundred thousand and ten million yoginīs, Pā Pū (5). [In the heart.]

Aiṁ (5) Hrīṁ Gāyatrī Nlūṁ! O you who enter the womb of the enjoyments of the Ratna-Nāga world; O Amṛtasaṃcāriṇī of the Ratna-Nāga world; O Goddess Nāgānanda, Mother of the Nāgas; O you who possess the siddhis of four hundred thousand koṭis; O Yoginī of four hundred thousand koṭis! Pā Pū (5). [Recite] at the navel.

Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ Alūṃ! O you who enter the womb of infinite enjoyment, the jewel sapphire; O you who move through the nectar of infinite worlds; O goddess of infinite bliss, mother of the infinite, possessor of infinite millions of billions of *siddhis*, infinite millions of billions of *yoginīs*—Pā Pū (5)! [Salutation] at the place of the head.
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ. To the venerable Ratnapañcakanyāsabhaṭṭāraka, Pā Pū (5). Bali! Thus is the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the Five Jewels.
In all worlds, beginning with the sky, the fruit that pervades is the removal of all sins; everyone obtains this merely by means of the ritual placement (*nyāsa*). This is the fruit of *nyāsa*.
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ, on the two feet of Anantagranthi: Pā Pū (5) || Pā Ḷ Niguli.
Aiṃ (5) Hāṃ, [I place] Kālagranthi on the two ankles; Pā Pū (5), [I place] Guṇṭhisaṇigu.
Aiṃ (5) Hiṃ: [the fierce knot] at the two shanks; Pā Pū (5): Chechenigu.
Aiṃ (5) Hīṃ, [to] the Jyeṣṭha-knot on the two thighs; Pā Pū (5).
The harsh words.
Aiṃ (5) Hūṃ at the left knot on both hips; Pā Pū (5) Kaḍacukanekhe.
Aiṁ (5) Hūṁ, at the tip of the *liṅga* is the Knot of Desire (*kāmagranthi*); Pā Pū (5). E, this is the *liṅga*-yācośa.
Aiṃ (5) Hṛṃ: at the location of the penis, the knot of the physical body; Pā Pū (5): at the forest of the navel.
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ, [seal] Brahmagranthi at the station of Brahman, Pā Pū (5), within the navel.
Aiṃ (5) Hḷaṃ, at the solar knot in the ocean of the navel: Pā Pū (5). [The navel.]
Aiṃ (5) Hḷṃ, [the knot of Soma] in the middle of the back, Pā Pū (5) || Khopatasa ||
Aiṃ (5) Heṃ, [seal] at the knot of the vital breath in the abdomen; Pā Pū (5) || Ghātasa.
Aiṃ (5) Haiṃ, the knot of life in the heart; Pā Pū (5), the essence of nectar.
Aiṃ (5) Hoṃ, the Viṣṇu-knot at the throat; Pā Pū (5). Kathuṣa.
Aiṁ (5) Hauṁ. The Rudra-knot is in the middle of the palate; Pā Pū (5) Thaṃkośa.
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ, the knot of Īśvara, at the location of the head; Pā Pū (5). For the head.
Aiṃ (5) Haṃḥ! At the location of the crown of the head is the knot of Sadāśiva; Pā Pū (5) Casaporasa.
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ (9). To the venerable Lord of the Knot-Installation, pā pū (5). [Offer] the bali.
Thus is the placement of the knots.
One should meditate on [the syllable] Aiṃ, resembling the rising sun, blazing with great splendor;
one should meditate on it as it pervades every station, illuminating the sixteen knots.
By this placement of the knots, one should accomplish immortality.
Success through speech, agitation of the city [of the body], and intense command arise. This is the fruit of the ritual placement (nyāsa).
Then follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the single-syllable mantra.
Aiṃ (5) Klīṃ on the two nostrils; Pā Pū (5) on the teeth, the palate, the throat, and the nails.
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ, in the mouth Pā Pū (5). Khvārasa.
Aiṃ (5) Yaṃ to the three eyes; Pā Pū (5) [to the heart]; Śikhā (3).
Aiṁ (5) Saṁḥ, to the Self of All, Pā Pū (5) || Sakabhinaṃ ||
Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ on both ears; Pā Pū (5) Hna Sa Pa Nne Khe.
Aiṁ (5) Aḥ on the two feet; Pā Pū (5) Pā Ḷne Pāṃ.
Aiṃ (5) Saṃ (9). This is the single-syllable placement (nyāsa) for the Venerable Lady (Bhaṭṭārikā); Pā Pū (5).
"Baliṃ"—this is the single-syllable placement (nyāsa).

One should daily perform the placement (*nyāsa*) of the single-syllable mantra (*ekākṣarī*) upon the excellent hand; I shall now declare the five great sins (*pañcapātaka*) that destroy minor offenses (*upapātaka*). [This is] the fruit of the placement.
Thus ends the destruction of evil dreams and sins through the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the single-syllable mantra.
Then follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the Praṇava.
Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ, Phaṭ to the weapon! Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) to the heart, salutation; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hrīṃ, svāhā to the head. Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śrīṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hsphreṃ, hūṃ for the armor; pā pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hsauṃ, Vaṣaṭ to the three eyes; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Aiṃ astrāya phaṭ pā pū (5) || And the offering (bali).
Thus concludes the ritual placement of the Praṇava.
The Praṇava, through the five-fold ritual placement (pañcanyāsa), destroys the five great sins;
on the five planes it yields auspicious fruit, and one obtains the fruit of the five groups. This is the fruit of the ritual placement.

Aiṃ (5) Hsaṃ, to the two thumbs, Pā Pū (5), and so forth; perform the ninefold placement (*navānyāsa*) as before. Aiṃ (5) Phaṃ (9) Saṃ (9), to the venerable Navātmānyāsa, Pā Pū (5). [Offer] the sacrificial oblation (*bali*).
Thus ends the Nyāsa of the Ninefold Self.
O Mistress of the Lords of Heroes, hear now this Nyāsa of the Navātman;
when this Nyāsa of the Navātman of great power is placed within one's body, [it grants liberation].
By the mere remembrance of this, the cage of sins is consumed;
before long, the perfection of the sky-farer (khecarī-siddhi) is attained, and the yoginī reaches a state of equanimity.
One should place the seed-syllables in their respective locations within the body. [The fruit of this ritual placement: Nyāsaphalam.
Then follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the Aghora-weapon mantra.
Aiṃ (5) Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Hrūṃ Prasphura (2) Hṛdayāya Namaḥ Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Ghore (2) Taratanu Rūpacaṭa Śirase Svāhā Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Caṭa (2) Pracaṭa (2) Śikhāyai Vaṣaṭ Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Kaha (2) Vama (2) Kavacāya Hūṃ Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Dama (2) Ghāṭaya (2) Vighātaya (2) Vauṣaṭ to the three eyes; Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Vighna (2) Hūṃ (3) Phaṭ! To the weapon, Phaṭ! Pā Pū (5)!
Aiṃ (5) Haṃ (9) Saṃ (9), to the body of the Aghora-weapon, to the venerable Nyāsa, Pā Pū (5).
Bali: The Aghora-weapon-mantra, when recited daily with offerings, is a constant warder-off of all weapons.
The fruit of the nyāsa. Thus ends the Aghora-kanyāsa.
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Śkṣmlvryīṃ. To the venerable Lord of the Sixfold Deposition (Ṣoḍhānyāsabhaṭṭāraka), Pā Pū (5).
Accept the offering, svāhā!
Thus, this sixfold nyāsa has been taught in the Western Tradition;
it clearly bestows the four aims of human life and destroys all obstacles.
One established in the ritual procedure of the Śrī-sāsana should perform the fourfold placement (nyāsa) upon the body;
he who does so will truly become Śaṅkara himself within a year.
The one who performs the ritual placement (nyāsa) should again bow to the Guru, who is like a father. By him, that which was clearly taught by the ancient sages according to their own vision—
namely, that which is devoid of all dualities and should be perpetually placed within the body— is [to be performed].
Day after day, his accumulated sins burn him.
Having bowed down to the Guru, as well as to his mother and father,
a man who is devoted to the sixteen-fold ritual placement (ṣoḍhānyāsa) [should do so] even if he is otherwise devoid of that ritual placement.
O Lord Pārvatī, one who bows down without performing the sixfold placement (ṣoḍhānyāsa) soon meets death and falls into hell. — *Vidyānanda*
Then, having formed the Nāda-mudrā with the left index finger using the Aghora-weapon mantra, one should hold a jewel and flowers.
Aiṁ (5) Hrāṁ Hrīṁ Hrūṁ Hraṁḥ Prasphura (2), etc. With this mantra, the sound-gesture (*nādamudrā*) should be bestowed while placing a single flower upon the head.
Then, one should perform worship upon one's own head by means of the lineage of gurus.

Aiṁ (5). To the venerable Gaṇanandadeva and the venerable Avirāmbā Devī, who are themselves Cāṭula and Aṭṭahāsā, [I offer] self-offering and worship. Aiṁ (5). To the venerable Garbhamuktānandadeva and Garbhāmbā Devī, who are themselves Cāṭula and Aṭṭahāsā, [I offer] self-offering and worship. (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Krīḍānandadeva, Samalāmbā Devī, Cāṭulā, Aṭṭahāsā—these five are themselves the Pāpū. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Sākānandadeva, Aṭṭahāsā, Ās, Svayaṃpā, Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Ānandadeva Aṭṭahāsā Asvayaṃ Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Sahajānandadeva, Aṭṭahāsā, Asvayaṃpā, Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Ṭīkānandadeva Aṭṭahāsā Asvayaṃpā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Dhanasānandadeva, Aṭṭahāsā, Svayaṃpā, Pū (5).
Aiṁ (5) Śrī Devānandadeva, Aṭṭahāsā, A-svayaṃpā, Pū (5).
Aiṁ (5). To the venerable Jvālānandadeva and Aṭṭahāsā, svayam-pūjā (5).
Aiṁ (5) Śrī-Yaśonandadeva, Aṭṭahāsā, Āsrayam, Pā, Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Aprabhānandadeva Aṭṭahāsāsvayaṃ Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ Pā Pū (5) || Baliṃ ||
Aiṃ (5) Aghore, Amoghe, Varade, Vīmale, Aṃ, to Brahmāṇī, Vicce, Pā, Pū (5).
Thus, and so forth, is the worship with the Mātṛkā mantra.
Aiṃ (5) Saṃ (9) Pā Pū (5) || Baliṃ ||
Aiṃ (5) HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ Ānandaśakti Bhairavānanda Vīrādhipataye ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ PĀ PŪ (5) || Aiṃ (5) ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ Śrīmahāvidyārājeśvarī HSKṢMLVRYŪṂ PĀ PŪ (5) ||
Three añjalis. (3)
aiṃ (5) hskṣmlvryūṃ śkṣmlvryīṃ pā pū (5) ||
The worship of Aghoravajravatī and Śrītrivatiśī.
Supreme Authority; Command; Nirvāṇa, the Root-Vidyā; the Six Traditions; the Supreme Syllable.
Mahānirvāṇa; the rites of invocation and so forth; sandalwood and so forth; incense; the five great mudrās.
The lotus, bow, vulva, and parasol are the great mudrās. One sprinkles [the disciple] on the head with a drop of water from the root arghya vessel.
Aiṃ (5) Kṣlūṃ Pā Pū (5) || Aiṃ (5) Kiṇi (2) Vicce Koṅkannāya Hraḥ Astrāya Phaṭ ||
The dismissal: Taking the flower situated on one's own head, [one regards it] as an ornament upon one's own head.
Something should be given to others even with a single flower.
Having smelled the remaining flower and having performed the offering of the bali-oblation;
In that regard, *tarpaṇa* (satiating): whether with water or with milk, it is *tarpaṇa*. *Śodhana* (purification).
Or the root-arghya vessel; the libation.
Aiṃ (5). The twenty-eighth maṇḍala, extracted from the sequence of twenty-eight [syllables].
Homage to you who abide as the Universal Monarch; homage to you, the Supreme Lord.
Salutations to you, Lord Bhairava; salutations to you, the bestower of knowledge.

I bow to this entire Kulacakra, which consists of eight groups of eight for the Baṭukas and likewise for the Yoginīs, as well as for the Kṣetrapālas, Gaṇas, and so forth, and for all the Gaṇapas— [all] of one single form.

May there be long life, health, sovereignty, progeny, wealth, prosperity, and the increase of lineage for ourselves and our retinues; for the sake of the desire for the aforementioned fruits, [we offer] obeisance to the Samayacakra.
Pā pū. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Salutation to the illustrious Nātha. Aiṃ (5) Salutation to the illustrious Siddhinātha.
Aiṃ (5). Homage to the illustrious Kujeśanātha. One should perform the formal acceptance.
One should offer three drops as before;
then, as previously described, perform the worship of the water-offering vessel (arghapātra).
The self-worship is as before, with the Nirvāṇa mantra.
Then follows the worship of the lineage of gurus.
Aiṃ (5), to the Support-Power (Ādhāraśakti) and the Lotus-Seated One (Kamalāsana), Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5). For the lotus posture, pā pū (5). Meditation.
Aiṁ (5): White in color, with two arms, holding a rosary for recitation in the right hand and an alms-bowl in the left hand, and clad in a garment of blue silk.
I bow to that Lord of the Sky (Gagaṇeśvara), who wears a black antelope skin as his upper garment and a deer-skin as his lower wrap,
who is seated in the lotus posture, and whose armpit holds a staff,
and who is worshipped everywhere by the gods.
Meditation is the flower; it is the vessel for purification. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Gaganānanda Deva and Avirāmbā Devī, Cāṭulā and Aṭṭahāsā, Svayam-pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śrīgarbhamuktānandadeva, Bhāgāmbā Devī, Cāṭule Aṭṭahāsā, Svayaṃ Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) Śrīkrīḍānandadeva, Samalāmbā Devī, Cāṭule Aṭṭahāsā, Svayaṃ Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5). To the illustrious Sākānandadeva and Aṭṭahāsā, Svayaṃpā, Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Ānandadeva, Aṭṭahāsā, Asvayaṃpā, Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śrī Sahajānandadeva, Aṭṭahāsā, Ās, Svayaṃpā, Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śrīṭakānandadeva, Aṭṭahāsā, Ās, Svayaṃpā, Pū (5).
Aiṁ (5) Śrī Dhanasānandadeva Aṭṭahāsā Sva-pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Devānandadeva, Aṭṭahāsā, Asvayaṃpā, Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Śrīyevejānandadeva Aṭṭahāsāsvayaṃ Pā Pū (5).
Aiṁ (5) Śrī Javvejānandadeva Aṭṭahāsā Sva-yaṃ Pā Pū (5).
Aiṁ (5) Śrī Aprabhānandadeva Aṭṭahāsāsvayaṃpā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hskṣmlvryūṃ, obeisance and worship (pā pū) to the venerable lineage of the twelve Gurus. (5)
Thus [one offers] the bali; one should display the dhenumudrā.
Thus concludes the worship of the lineage of gurus.
Then follows the worship of the medicinal herbs (auṣadhīpūjana).
Aiṃ (5) To the lotus seat, pā pū (5). Aiṃ (5) To the petal seat, pā pū (5). Aiṃ (5) To the pericarp seat, pā pū (5). Aiṃ (5) To the corpse seat, pā pū (5).
Meditative concentration.
Aiṃ (5). Seated comfortably upon a lotus throne, she is white in color and possesses three eyes;
she has three faces, and is beautifully adorned with red, white, and yellow [complexions].
O great hero with eight arms, you hold a sword and a threatening gesture,
a hand-drum, a trident, a sacred thread, and a blue lotus with its stalk.
She who has drops on her bowl, excellent hands, and full, elevated breasts,
should be understood from the context of medicinal rites as one who lives long through her livelihood.
The flower of meditative concentration, Pā Pū. (5)
Aiṃ (5) Hsphrāṃ Sarvajanakṣobhaṇī Pā Pū (5) ||
Aiṃ (5) Hsphrīṃ, O you who enchant all people, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hsphrū, O crusher of all people, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hsphraiṃ, the paralyzer of all people, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hsphrauṃ, O you who attract all people, Pā Pū (5).
Aiṃ (5) Hsphraṃḥ! O you who entice all people and the lowly, Pā Pū (5)!
Aiṃ (5) ŚKṢMLVRYĪṂ, obeisance (pā pū) to the venerable one of the medicinal tradition (auṣadhīkramabhaṭṭārakāya). (5)
This is the *bali* offering. The *yonimahāmudrā*. The practice for deluding (*mohanī-sādhana*) is in that very same place.
Thus ends the worship of the medicinal herbs.
Then follows the worship of Śrīkaṇṭha.
Aiṃ (5) for the bull-throne, Pā Pū (5). Aiṃ (5) for the lion-throne, Pā Pū (5).
Meditative absorption.
Aiṁ (5). The God seated upon a bull and a lion, resembling a snow-mountain or the moon, with one face and three eyes, possessing a divine form and great brilliance.
The Great Lord has four arms and holds a trident and an eye;
following behind the Goddess at her side, he bears a linga, a skull-cup, and a full vessel.
Holding the chin of the Goddess with his left hands, he supports her;
the Goddess, dark-limbed and in the bloom of youth, has come to rest upon his left thigh.
The goddess has hands granting boons and fearlessness, possesses three eyes, and has a divine form;
her limbs are adorned with divine jewel-ornaments, and she is beautified by divine garments.
Having thus meditated upon Mahādeva, Śrīkaṇṭha, the Supreme Lord.
The flower of meditative concentration, Pā Pū. (5)

Aiṃ (5). Pūrṇeśa has a white lotus seat and a bird-like face; he is white in color, three-eyed, and holds in his right hands a rosary, a fine bell, an arrow, a goad, and the gesture of fearlessness;
in his left hands, he bears a trident, a noose, a bow, a well-directed thunderbolt, and a garland of severed heads.
And thus one meditates upon the god Lalita, who has ten arms and wears a serpent as a sacred thread.
Pūrṇeśī sits upon a corpse-throne; she has six faces, is dark-complexioned, and possesses three eyes.
Above that, her [face] is golden-colored, and further above that, it is pure white on the right.
Her northern face has a blue luster, is white when seen, and has the appearance of a fresh, unopened *javā* flower; she wears a garland of severed heads.
Her limbs are adorned with eight serpents, and her sandals, held by the rays of the sun, possess a beauty that is licked by [the light].
She who holds in her right hands a skull-cup, a mirror, a noose, a bell, a spear, and a discus; in another hand she holds a jar of nectar, and in yet another a khaṭvāṅga staff;
furthermore, she bears a noose, a formidable rosary, and a very white conch shell.
One should meditate with focused yoga upon that goddess, who bestows happiness and is adorned in all her limbs.

Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hsphreṃ Hsauṃ! All the primary seats (pīṭhas) and secondary seats (upapīṭhas), as well as the gates and sub-gates, the fields (kṣetras) and sub-fields (upakṣetras), and the great assemblies (saṃdohas) situated in every direction.
The yoginīs and the lords of the heroes of yoga have all assembled here at this festival of the great wheel; may Śrīnātha grant me his boon.
O Goddess, for those who are devoted to the Teaching and intent upon the worship of the Guru’s feet,
may my grace of all supernatural attainments (siddhis) always be theirs.
O Goddess, those on this earth who hate the heroes and the yoginīs, they [become] there at the end, an offering (bali) in the assembly of the conduct of the *samaya*.
O you who are thronged by hosts of Yoginīs, you who cut away the hearing, memory, mental nourishment, flesh, fat, bone, and life-force of the wicked!
May the hosts of Yoginīs, who are crowded with troops, destroy the deceits of the wicked, such as sorcery, bad dreams, and the speech of ill omens.
The three seats beginning with Oṃkāra are proclaimed as Sālā;
they are the collections of medicinal herbs and minerals located in the ten directions and the intermediate directions.
In the earth, the netherworld, the cosmic egg, and in all other places,
the practitioners whose souls are united with yoga abide as equals alongside the Yoginīs.
O lords of great heroes, the deities abide in truth;
so too do the Siddhas, the Putrakas, the Ācāryas, the Sādhakas, and those who sleep upon the earth.
Whether in a city or a village, in a forest or by an excellent river,
at a pond, a well, a solitary tree, or in a cremation ground or a circle of Mothers.
Others too, assuming various forms and dwelling in banyan trees,
may they all be satisfied and accept the offering from every side.
Even though I have come for refuge, may all this grant them its fruit:
whatever action has been performed by me, whatever I shall do, and whatever has already been done.
May my protectors be satisfied by this offering of flowers;
may all my activities be accomplished, and may all my faults be pacified.
By the grace of Śiva and Śakti, I bow to the eight verses of the venerable Kubjikā.
Thus is the *samayabali*.
Now, as for old age and so forth.

Vīrabhadra, Mahākālī, Kaṅkālī, Vikṛtānanā, Koṭalā, Bhīmabhadra, Vāyuvegā, and Bhayānanā. (8)

O Goddess, Great Yoginī, always accept this *bali* offering from me!

I bow to the Goddess of gods, who is joined with Ularaka in the lotuses of the heart. || 1 ||
She who exists in the earth, heaven, and the intermediate space; in the world of the ten directions; at the root of the seven netherworlds;

in the sacred fields (*kṣetra*), the seats (*pīṭha*), and the secondary seats (*upapīṭha*); in the uneven four seats, the meeting places (*melaka*), Kailāsa, and the cremation grounds (*śmaśāna*); on the banks of the Indus, under a solitary tree, on the auspicious shore of the ocean, and in the descent of the Smoke-colored One (*dhūmakālāvatāra*).
In Kaulūla, in Pūrṇagiri, in Aṅga, in the preeminent city of Gaṇa, and in the principal Oḍiyāna. (2)
In the city of Kulapati known as Jāla, the foremost of yogic seats; in Kāmarūpa, which is one's own true nature;
in Ujjayinī, Aṭṭahāsa, Paṭupaṭa, Sahakela, and the region of Ḍāha;
at Śrīśaila, Pārijāta, the abode of Paśupati, and on the slopes of the Golden Vindhya mountains.
In the land of Ugradeśa, on Mount Marutapatha, [reside] Śrīmelā, Lākinī, and Sākinī. (3)
In Kaśmīra, in the land of Candra, in Draviḍa, Malaya, Ṭha, Brahmāvarta, Kulūta, Strīrājya, Harkka, Trukka, Urasi, Virajaka, Siddhikṣetra,
Uhāla, Kaulagiri, Devikoṭa, on the peak of Himagiri, in the land of Kāñcī, and at Prayāga.
In Saurāṣṭra, in the Middle Country (Madhyadeśa), in the city of Bhṛgukaccha, in Kauśala, or in Kāmraka. || 4 ||

May all the Mothers—Yoni, Jā, Maṇḍajā, and Āmbā—who are praised by various wise ones, protect us all in these places: at Karṇānta, Koṅkaṇa, or the excellent city of Magadha; at Karṇakubja in Kaliṅga; at Liṅgotra; in the midst of the sky; and at the site called Gahvara, the bed of the best of gods.
May the Siddhas, the Tuṣṭas, and the Susiddhas—praised by various wise ones—grant divine accomplishments. (5)
The sword, or the accomplishment of mantra, entry into another's body, the power of moving through the sky, or divine vision;

the paralyzing of weapons, the subjugation of enemies, the attainment of strength and victory, and the mastery of all sciences; long life, poetic talent, the alchemical elixir, the magic pill, the sandals, and the accomplishment of all desires.
May all the Bhairavas, joined with their consorts, who consume flesh, fat, and blood, grant all that is inconceivable. || 6 ||
May Carmamuṇḍā dispel fear in the midst of wicked beings, thieves, enemies, pestilence, the multitude of planets, lightning strikes, battle, royal courts, or floods of water; she who,
laughing with "ha ha ha ha" and uttering "chāṃ chīṃ pheṭ," devours and drinks [the enemy].
The Mother of Mantras is satisfied, uttering the Kaula language: *kili mili cikili*.
She is withered, possessing the form of desire; she has the sounds of *ra*, *la*, *va*, *śa*, *ṣa*, *ha*, *hā*, *hā*, *ha*, and *hūṃ*;
she rises up, blue-throated, compassionate toward both asuras and suras, marked by the *bindu*, and fierce yet praiseworthy.
Uttering *phreṃ phreṃ pheṭ* with a roar, she is smeared with the blood and fat of the *ruru* deer, her limbs stained with color.
The auspicious world-protectors, numbering eight hundred million, are joined with the earthly [element] and not associated with any other. (8)

May that renowned power of Rudra grant auspiciousness; may the terrifying Cāmuṇḍā, whose form is perfection and whose form is black, manifest in the ten directions; may those known as Kuṇḍalā and Mālinī—eternally joined with the ether, who have subdued the hosts of the ocean and whose bodies are the point (bindu)—be celebrated.
Always abiding in the garden, those consisting of both the Kula and Akula have entered the wheel of yoga. (9)

Illuminating the kingdom of women, she who is without beginning or end, having pierced through the various successions of others, is the divine command; she is the guardians of the world, pervading all things, born of the sacred seats (pīṭha), and known as Maṅgalā.
She, the mother of the three worlds, resides within the wheel of the command (ājñācakra) in the center of the seat of Śrīkaṇṭha.
The goddess of gods, the pacifier on the path of Śiva, [is the power] that destroys the path of Time. (10)

Known by the name Śrī Kubjikā, she whose body is curved, who is the seat and sub-seat of mantra, resides in the south as Siddhiyoginī; she is conjoined with the Sun (Ravi), the Maṇḍalā of the Pūrṇa-pīṭha.
Known as Kāmākhyā and Koṅkaṇā, she is established in many lineages and various forms within the accomplishment of knowledge.
May the Vasudhā, known as the lineage of the Fortune of Liberation, be victorious in the netherworld, on earth, and in heaven. || 11 ||

Arise! You who cause the upward scripture to throb, you who subdue all things, the fierce one (*raudrī*), whose bowstring is the syllable *hūṃ*, blazing and burning intensely, established in the full moon;
she is the eldest, the left, the fierce one, stationed together with *ḍa-la-ra-ka* in the sevenfold division.
Satisfied with the fivefold division, they belong to the stainless family; all together, they are the five jewels. || 12 ||
She is one, yet manifold in her divisions; she flows through the triple path (Tripathagā); she is the woman who possesses eight mothers of the hair-pores.
She is Jṛmbhā, Jṛmbhā, Sujṛmbhā, Calā, Calavalicālā, and Prasphurantī; she is the three triangles.
Bestowing peace and accomplishment, she consists of blood, flesh, and fat; she is the most excellent among all, abiding in the highest place.
Raining down divine commands with the sounds *phaphaphaphaphasa*, she utters the *phe* and *pheṭkāra* sounds. || 13 ||
